results.title: Ghana World Cup 2026 Group L Preview: Black Stars Face England, Croatia and Panama Without Kudus - Nigerian Matchday
highlights:
Ghana’s path to the 2026 World Cup was one of the most impressive in the entire CAF qualifying campaign. Carlos Queiroz, the experienced Portuguese coach who previously managed Iran and Saudi Arabia at multiple World Cups, brought structure and tactical discipline to a squad that struggled for consistency in previous cycles. Eight wins from ten qualifying games, with Jordan Ayew contributing seven goals as captain, tells the story of a confident, cohesive unit. That qualifying form gives them real belief — even with Kudus missing.
[...]
The route to the round of 16 runs through beating Panama and securing at least one point from the England and Croatia games. With the expanded 48-team format allowing third-placed finishers to progress, even a point or two could be enough. On one hand, the Black Stars possess Premier League-level talent throughout the squad and comfortably qualified for the tournament. On the other, managerial upheaval, inconsistent performances and uncertainty over key players have created concern among supporters.

Reaching the knockout rounds would represent a successful tournament given the circumstances. Anything beyond that would be viewed as a major achievement. Yet Ghana’s World Cup history has repeatedly shown that writing off the Black Stars can be a dangerous mistake.
